data.title: Blue Jays in bidding war with Cubs, Orioles, Giants for $12.5M ex-Dodgers 4x World Series champion - Sporting News
data.content: The Toronto Blue Jays weren't happy with how last season unfolded, especially after coming off a World Series appearance the year before. Toronto's biggest issue throughout the 2026 campaign was the number of injuries that plagued its starting rotation. The top of Toronto's rotation appears to be relatively set, but figuring out the final spots could be a challenge for the organization. “The Toronto Blue Jays’ rotation was ravaged by injuries in 2026, showcasing that health is never a given in the game of baseball. While Dylan Cease, José Soriano, and Trey Yesavage should make for a strong top half of Toronto’s rotation in 2027, the rest of the options to fill out the final two spots come with a lot of question marks,” Blue Jays Nation’s Michael Coyle wrote. If the Blue Jays can land him and he returns to his best form, he could give Toronto a formidable first four in its starting rotation.

data.title: Braves predicted to sign $22M All-Star southpaw with elite command to pair with Chris Sale - Sporting News
data.content: # Braves predicted to sign $22M All-Star southpaw with elite command to pair with Chris Sale. The Atlanta Braves head into what could be a pivotal offseason as they look to defend their NL East title for the first time in several seasons. Chris Sale is the only member of the current rotation who appears to be a lock to be there on Opening Day. “While it wasn't their downfall in the end, the starting rotation has been a constant thorn in the Atlanta Braves' side for multiple seasons now. “The good news, and the reason I think the Braves should take a flyer on the southpaw, is that Atlanta pitching coach Jeremy Hefner proved to be something of a secret weapon for the team in 2026. And if he could, Imanaga is exactly what the Braves need: an affordable veteran lefty to back up Chris Sale who keeps strikeouts high and walks low,” Janeiro wrote.
